title: Send the shelf-label printer exactly what it reads

blocks.text: The shelf-label printer in warehouse 3 has started printing labels whose fields drift to the left, and some labels come out blank. Its manual is strict about the job it receives: a setup command on one line, then the label's body, where every line is a field exactly 24 characters wide, padded with spaces on the right, and every line ends with a line break.
For the label on aisle B, shelf 07, the setup command is
and the body's three fields are `AISLE B / SHELF 07`, `SKU 44-1093` and `QTY 12`.

The team's style rule allows 60 columns per source line, so the setup command can't sit on one line. Write both `TODO` methods of `src/main/java/practice/ShelfLabel.java` as text blocks: when you're done, `job()` returns the exact characters the manual asks for. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: the print job holds the setup command and the three body fields in order
every body line keeps its padding to 24 characters and ends with a line break
the setup command, written over several source lines, arrives as one line with nothing added at the joins

origin.section: A Backslash at the End of a Line Removes the Line Break and Nothing Else

concepts: A backslash at the end of a line removes the line break and adds nothing; extra indentation of the continued line stays in the value.
Trailing spaces typed in a text block are stripped; a \s at the end of the line keeps them, because it is not whitespace when the stripping happens.
